blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A sales deck in late 2026 says a commercial MIP solver 'tops Mittelmann's MILP benchmark today'. What does that benchmark's site, as read in this lesson, let a reviewer conclude?

options.text: The claim is confirmed there, since the commercial solvers head the current MILP table
options.says: The current MILP table lists COPT, SCIP, FiberSCIP, HiGHS and Optverse; Gurobi, CPLEX and Xpress are not in it.

options.text: The claim cannot be checked there, since the three commercial results were withdrawn
options.says: Right: IBM and FICO had their results removed after 2018, and Gurobi withdrew in August 2024.

options.text: The claim is refuted there, since an open-source solver heads the current MILP table
options.says: A table without the commercial solvers cannot refute a claim about them; it simply does not include them.

options.text: The claim is confirmed there, since the vendors publish their own rows in the MILP table
options.says: Vendors agreed only to aggregated results on the MIPFEAS page, as one virtual solver; the MILP table has no commercial rows.

origin.section: Public Benchmarks Compare Only Open-Source Solvers, Because the Commercial Three Withdrew

questions.stem: Solver A and solver B both prove the same optimum on one model. A reports 5,000 LP iterations, B reports 15,000. What do the two counts tell you about which solver did less work?

options.text: A did about a third of B's work, since both counted the same simplex steps
options.says: Each solver's LP iterations come from its own LP solver on its own subproblems; the counts are not the same unit.

options.text: B did about three times A's work, since its count shows three times as many pivots
options.says: Same mistake from the other side: a count compares runs of one solver, never two solvers.

options.text: A ran about three times faster, since iterations convert to seconds at one fixed rate
options.says: No fixed rate links a count to seconds, and the counts belong to different solvers.

options.text: Nothing on that question, since each solver counts its work in its own unit
options.says: Right: the lesson's rule is never to compare one solver's count with another's.

origin.section: In the Runner, Four Solvers Solve GridCap's Selection Model to the Same Optimum

questions.stem: A maximization model has one continuous variable. Through MathOpt, HiGHS and SCIP both report OPTIMAL with 41.37, and CP-SAT reports OPTIMAL with 40.00. What best explains CP-SAT's lower value?

options.text: CP-SAT rounded the continuous variable to an integer, so it solved another model
options.says: Right: the lesson's continuous probe shows CP-SAT returning a = 8 and 19.68 against the true 20.3078.

options.text: CP-SAT kept the continuous variable and found a better plan the others missed
options.says: In a maximization a lower value is a worse plan, and two solvers proved 41.37 optimal.

options.text: CP-SAT stopped at its default gap, leaving the continuous variable short of its best
options.says: The lesson's probe shows CP-SAT at its answer with a = 8: the variable was rounded, not the search stopped early.

options.text: CP-SAT searched the continuous variable from another seed and ended at another optimum
options.says: A seed changes the path, not the optimal value; two different optimal values mean two different models.
